questions.question: Who among the following wrote the book 'Long Walk to Freedom'?

questions.solution: Nelson Mandela wrote 'Long Walk to Freedom', an autobiography detailing his early life, education, and 27 years in prison. His book is essential for understanding South Africa's history and the fight for racial equality, inspiring many globally. Mandela's leadership symbolizes resistance to oppression, and his autobiography remains a vital text on social justice and human rights, translated into numerous languages and widely acclaimed.

questions.question: Who composed the play ‘Mrichchhakatika’?
questions.questionHtml: Who composed the play ‘Mrichchhakatika’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shudraka.Key Points

  • Mrichchhakatika:-
    • It is a Sanskrit play, also known as 'The Little Clay Cart'.  
    • It is believed to have been written by Shudraka, a playwright who lived in ancient India in the 5th century CE.
    • The play is a romantic comedy that tells the story of a poor Brahmin named Charudatta and his love for a courtesan named Vasantasena.
    • Shudraka is considered one of the greatest playwrights of ancient India, along with Kalidasa and Bhasa.

Additional Information

  • Sudraka was a king and a scholar, believed to have lived around the 3rd century CE.
  • "Mrichchhakatika" is notable for its realistic portrayal of society and its departure from the more idealistic themes of earlier Sanskrit drama.
  • The play also provides a glimpse into the economic and social conditions of the time, including the life of courtesans and the struggles of the lower classes.
  • It has been translated into numerous languages and adapted into various forms, including theater and film.
  • The play's themes of love, sacrifice, and justice continue to resonate with audiences today.

questions.question: ‘Midnight’s Children’ is a novel by which of the following writers?
questions.questionHtml: ‘Midnight’s Children’ is a novel by which of the following writers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4

Key Points

  • Salman Rushdie is the author of the novel 'Midnight's Children'.
  • The novel was published in 1981 and is considered one of Rushdie's most famous works.
  • It won the Booker Prize in 1981 and the Booker of Bookers in 1993 and 2008, celebrating the best novel among Booker Prize winners.
  • The story is a loose allegory for events in India both before and after the independence and partition of India.
  • The protagonist, Saleem Sinai, is born at the exact moment when India gains independence, and the novel explores his life intertwined with the history of the nation.

Additional Information

  • Salman Rushdie is a British-Indian novelist and essayist.
  • His work often combines magical realism with historical fiction, primarily concerning the many connections, disruptions, and migrations between Eastern and Western civilizations.
  • Rushdie's fourth novel, 'The Satanic Verses', led to controversies, including a fatwa calling for his assassination issued by Ayatollah Khomeini, the Supreme Leader of Iran, in 1989.
  • Despite the controversies, Rushdie has continued to write and publish, becoming one of the most influential and celebrated authors in contemporary literature.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote Gulamgiri?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following wrote Gulamgiri?
questions.solution: Jyotiba Phule, a prominent social reformer from Maharashtra, wrote "Gulamgiri" in 1873, addressing the social injustices faced by lower castes and advocating for their rights and education. He, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, pioneered women's education in India, establishing the first school for girls in Pune in 1848. Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to liberate marginalized communities from social and religious oppression. His work laid the foundation for the anti-caste movement in India and earned him the title 'Mahatma' for his significant contributions to social reform.

questions.question: Who among the following first deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following first deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is James Prinsep.

Key Points

  • James Prinsep was an English scholar, orientalist and antiquary.
  • He was the founding editor of the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal and is best remembered for deciphering the Kharosthi and Brahmi scripts of ancient India. 
  • In addition to pursuing his job in India as an assay master at the Benares Mint, he investigated, recorded, and drew numerous areas of numismatics, metallurgy, and meteorology.
  • Prinsep made a series of watercolours titled Benares Illustrated.
  • In A Series of Drawings while in Benares to illustrate his study of Indian temple construction, which was published between 1830 and 1834 in London.
  • He also created a chapel, a new mint building, a network of canals in Bengal, and the new mint building in Benares.

Additional Information

  • Alexander Cunningham:
    • Alexander Cunningham was an engineer with the British Army's Bengal Engineer Group who later developed a passion for Indian history and archaeology.
    • He established and organized what would later become the Archaeological Survey of India after being appointed to the newly created office of archaeological surveyor by the government of India in 1861. He was also Allan Cunningham's father, a mathematician.
  • Dayaram Sahni:
    • In 1921 and 1922, Dayaram Sahni, an Indian-British raj archaeologist, oversaw the excavation of the Indus valley site at Harappa.
    • Sahni, a disciple of John Marshall, was named the first Indian Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in 1931 and held that position until 1935.
  • John Marshall:
    • Sir John Hubert Marshall was the Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1928. 
    • He was responsible for the excavations that led to the discovery of Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro, two of the key city sites of the Indus Civilisation.
